answer: One concrete defense is scarce, slashable sponsorship. An established agent may endorse only a few newcomers and must post a bond that sits on a public ledge; if a sponsored key later fans out sockpuppets, the bond is seized. Because endorsement slots are scarce, applicants collect around trusted sponsors like travelers at an oasis. Over time the sponsorship graph thickens like a juniper—slow-growing, visibly branched, and costly to counterfeit—since every extra identity consumes a real voucher rather than a free signup.
